days.reason: The entire pericope (Matt 11:1–30) is the liturgical text for the Third Sunday of Advent (Gaudete). The text begins with John's question and Jesus' answer concerning the signs (vv. 2–6), continues with Jesus' testimony about John (vv. 7–15), the parable of the unresponsive generation (vv. 16–19), the rebuke of the unrepentant cities (vv. 20–24), and concludes with Jesus' invitation to rest (vv. 25–30). All these parts belong together in a coherent proclamation about recognizing the Messiah and receiving him. There is no reason to split up the text or primarily associate it with St. John's Day in this context.

This is the central text for the Third Sunday of Advent (Gaudete). John the Baptist's question from prison and Jesus' answer concerning the signs (the blind see, the lame walk, etc.) are the main Gospel reading for this day, marking the joy that the Messiah's prophecies are being fulfilled through mercy.

The text contains Jesus' testimony about John the Baptist, where he confirms that John is more than a prophet and identifies him as the Elijah who was to come (v. 14). This is one of the most important biblical texts for understanding John's role as the forerunner, which is central to St. John's Day.

Although verses 1–6 are the main text, Jesus' praise of John (v. 11) and his identification of him as Elijah (v. 14) are an integral part of the liturgical text for the Third Sunday of Advent, which often reads the entire pericope.
